diagnosis.root_cause:
Commit 6cd5503 added a module-level `_RECENT` dict to patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py. It is used as a response cache with no size limit and no eviction.

Every request with a new (collection, top_k, model, normalized question) key stores a new entry: the full response (raw_chunks with full chunk text, the assembled context and sources) plus `list(query_emb)`, which is about 768 boxed Python floats. These entries are never removed, so resident memory grows in proportion to the number of distinct questions served. That matches the monotonic RSS climb from 103 MB to 317 MB after the 10:14 deploy. The 6x traffic surge only speeds this up.

The cache is also a correctness hazard. Its key ignores knowledge-base changes, so it can serve stale context after ingestion.

This is a code defect, not a capacity problem. Two fixes would work:
- Smallest safe fix: remove the cache (revert 6cd5503).
- Alternative: cap it (for example an insertion-ordered dict limited to 256 entries that evicts the oldest) and stop storing the redundant `query_embedding` list.

Either keeps module-state growth well below the acceptance threshold of 1500 entries for 3000 questions. A restart is needed afterwards to reclaim memory that has already leaked.
evidence: patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py:67-68: `_RECENT: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}` at module level, with no max size or eviction anywhere in the file
patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py:76-78: the key is collection:top_k:model:question.lower(), so every distinct question adds a new key; a hit returns the cached object
patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py:106: `_RECENT[key] = {**response, "query_embedding": list(query_emb)}` stores raw_chunks, the assembled context and a full embedding copy on every miss
patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py:97-105: the response includes raw_chunks (full chunk text) and assembled_context, which makes each entry large

faults/acceptance/test_f4_memory_leak.py:27-32: the test sends 3000 distinct questions and requires module-level container growth < 1500 entries, which fails with the current unbounded dict (3000 entries)
Incident metrics: process_memory_mb{retrieval} 102.7 -> 317.1, rising monotonically since the 10:14:15Z deploy of 6cd5503, while other services stay flat
